- File: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py, .claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: _is_heredoc_operator, _is_redirect
  Problem: The docstring for _is_heredoc_operator claims support for the <<- heredoc operator, but the implementation of _is_redirect rejects it because the token contains a hyphen (-), which is not included in the allowed character set set("<>&").
  Why it fails at runtime: Inline-interpreter-write commands that use the <<- heredoc operator are not correctly identified as inline-interpreter-write commands by _segment_is_inline_write because has_heredoc is evaluated as False. This causes the permission prompt for such commands to be bypassed, creating a security risk.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- File: workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py
  Line or code reference: lines 350-352, the new `_is_heredoc_operator` docstring; function body matches `_is_redirect` (lines 346-347) by calling it first.
  Problem: The new docstring claims `A \`<<\` or \`<<-\` heredoc operator`, but the body only matches `<<` (and `<<-…` variants where `-` is followed only by other heredoc text — none of which `set(token) <= set("<>&")` admits). Concretely, `_is_redirect("<<-")` returns False because `-` is not in `set("<>&")`, so `_is_heredoc_operator("<<-")` always returns False. The same is true in the `.claude/scripts/permission_prompts.py` twin.
  Why it fails at runtime: No behaviour change today — `_split_redirects` and the pre-PR `command_class` count also gated on `_is_redirect` and therefore never counted `<<-`. The new docstring, however, newly documents a capability the function does not have. A future reader relying on it (e.g. someone wiring up a new caller that passes `<<-` tokens through) would assume `<<-` heredoc bodies are counted and bound, when they are silently dropped (and the `aligned` count disagreement will then trigger the "bind nothing" fail-safe). The PR description explicitly lists `<<-` as out of project scope ("Not fixed (needs a decision or out of reach)"), so the docstring overstates what was shipped.
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
  SEVERITY: NIT
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
